verdict: The sub-square criterion WORKS: even though Pythia-410M is fully collapsed at the square point (Exp 33a), measuring lambda_min at T=d_head/2 predicts head importance at the square point (pearson 0.236, perm p=0.018; spearman 0.365). The collapse is head-stable across T (H2, r=0.66, p<0.0001). Operational recipe for deep models: measure at sub-square, prune at square.
honest_label: H1 failed as pre-registered (all heads already collapsed at T=32 — Pythia-410M is deeper in the collapse regime than expected), but H2/H3 show the HEAD-LEVEL collapse signature is stable and functionally meaningful. The criterion survives via H2+H3, not via H1. Single model, 96-head ablation subset.
